data.why: A photoelectric smoke detector hangs cut open on a living room wall above a burning trash can, with a hand at its test button; the smoke is followed from the fire up into the vents, across the beam onto the sensor and out as sound from the horn, and then its battery. The camera opens close on the dark box and its beam, steps back to show the fire and the smoke, and ends on the hand pressing test.

recurring.what: a hand at the test button

chain.shows: smoke from a burning trash can drifts through the beam and nothing happens
the sensor sees the smoke but the room fills in silence
dust and bugs drift in and the horn blares for nothing
behind the mesh screen the battery dies and the beam goes dark
the battery chirp at night gets the battery pulled out

surprises.claim: A photoelectric smoke detector shines a light beam away from a sensor; smoke scatters the light onto the sensor and sets off the alarm.
surprises.search: photoelectric smoke detector light scattered onto sensor how it works

surprises.claim: Smoke alarms must sound at least 85 decibels at 10 feet.
surprises.search: smoke alarm 85 decibels at 10 feet UL 217

surprises.claim: Fire safety agencies say to test smoke alarms once a month by pressing the test button.
surprises.search: test smoke alarms monthly test button NFPA USFA

sentences.text: If you shine a light across a dark box, you have a smoke detector.
But smoke drifts through the beam, and nothing happens.
So a side sensor catches light the smoke scatters.
But the sensor stays silent while everyone sleeps.
So you add a horn that blares 85 decibels.
This is a photoelectric smoke detector.
But the horn also blares at dust and bugs inside.
So a fine mesh screen keeps them out.
But behind that screen, the battery quietly dies.
So it chirps when the battery runs low.
But a chirp at 3 AM gets the battery pulled.
So you add a test button to check it monthly.
Press test, and the light flashes as it screams.
Congratulations, you built a smoke detector.
